The authors evaluate the attack against four generative models (CTGAN, TVAE, WGAN-GP, WGAN-WC) trained on three real-world datasets, measuring both synthetic data utility and attack success, and also test differential-privacy mitigations. CTGAN and TVAE are implemented by directly using the CTGANSynthesizer and TVAESynthesizer modules from SDGym, making them two of the four target/victim generative models whose synthetic data is attacked and analyzed throughout the empirical study.

title: TabMDA: Tabular Manifold Data Augmentation for Any Classifier using Transformers with In-context Subsetting
summary: This paper proposes TabMDA, a training-free manifold data augmentation method that uses a pre-trained in-context tabular model (e.g., TabPFN) to embed and augment training data via repeated in-context encoding with varied data subsets, improving performance for any downstream classifier across tabular datasets. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of the computationally expensive generative modeling approaches to tabular data augmentation that the paper's method avoids, with no experiment using it.

title: TabSCM: A practical Framework for Generating Realistic Tabular Data
summary: TabSCM is a mixed-type tabular data generator that preserves causal structure by orienting a CPDAG into a DAG, fitting root-node marginals, and learning topologically ordered structural assignments via conditional diffusion models and gradient-boosted trees, enabling counterfactual queries and fairness auditing. It is evaluated against GAN, diffusion, and LLM baselines on seven public datasets for statistical fidelity, downstream utility, and privacy. CTGAN is run as one of several baseline generators using its default parameter set, and SDMetrics' statistical-similarity and classifier-two-sample-test methodology is used to evaluate all generators including TabSCM.

title: TabSyM: A Generative Pipeline for Small Multi-Cohort Omics Tabular Data
summary: This preprint proposes TabSyM, a modular generative pipeline for small, high-dimensional, multi-cohort omics tabular data that combines an extended diffusion model (TabDDPM), a Bayesian-optimization-guided task-aware sampling mechanism, and a Multi-Domain Adversarial Network for cross-cohort alignment, validated on gastric-cancer survival prediction from scRNA-seq data. The pipeline's headline generator is TabDDPM, not any SDV-family model. CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) is cited among the SDV-family works but the abstract gives no indication it was run or compared against in the reported experiments.

title: TabuLa: Harnessing Language Models for Tabular Data Synthesis
summary: This paper proposes Tabula, a tabular data synthesizer built on a large-language-model architecture that discards pretrained NLP weights and introduces token sequence compression and a customized padding strategy to cut training time while preserving synthetic data utility. It is evaluated against five state-of-the-art tabular synthesizers on six datasets for both ML utility and training-time efficiency. CTGAN is run as one of the baseline generators in these experiments, with its conditional vector and mode-specific preprocessing discussed as prior art that Tabula's LLM-based approach departs from.

title: A Tabular Conditional Generative Adversarial Imputation Network for Vertical Federated Learning
summary: This preprint proposes a tabular conditional generative adversarial imputation network designed for missing-data imputation in a vertical federated learning setting, where feature partitions are distributed across multiple parties. The work appears to build a GAN-based imputation architecture tailored to tabular data and federated constraints. It cites the TGAN paper as related prior work on tabular GAN design, with no evidence available on whether TGAN's code or architecture was actually run or adopted.

title: Tabular GANs for Uneven Distribution
summary: This work surveys generative approaches to tabular data synthesis and proposes an experimental pipeline that augments a training set with GAN-generated rows to counter distribution shift between train and test data, evaluating downstream classifier performance across several configurations. The later full-text version expands this into a broader survey and modular framework spanning GANs, diffusion models, and LLMs, with a 'GAN backend' implementing CTGAN-style architecture. The authors explicitly took CTGAN's published GitHub source code and, with slight modification, used it as the generator underlying their augmentation experiments, describing its mode-specific normalization and conditional-vector training-by-sampling mechanism in detail.

title: Tabular Data Generation using Binary Diffusion
summary: This paper introduces a lossless binary transformation for tabular data and a new diffusion-based generative model, Binary Diffusion, that uses XOR noise operations and binary cross-entropy loss to avoid the complex preprocessing typical of tabular generators. It evaluates the new model against several state-of-the-art baselines on datasets like Travel, Adult Income, and Diabetes, showing smaller model size and competitive or better performance. TVAE, CopulaGAN, and CTGAN from the SDV family are run as baseline generators, trained with default settings (batch size 500, 200 epochs) alongside GReaT and Distill-GReaT for comparison.

title: Tabular Data Generation Models: An In-Depth Survey and Performance Benchmarks with Extensive Tuning
summary: This paper benchmarks five families of tabular data generation models (TVAE, CTGAN, TabDDPM, TabSyn, and SMOTE variants) across 16 diverse datasets, with extensive hyperparameter, encoding, and architecture tuning to determine how much dataset-specific optimization improves synthetic data quality and cost. It finds that diffusion-based models generally outperform others but that the advantage shrinks under a fixed GPU budget, and proposes reduced hyperparameter search spaces that retain most of the performance at far lower tuning cost. CTGAN and a customized TVAE are run as two of the five benchmarked generator families, their original cluster-based (mode-specific) normalization is examined and re-tuned, and the SDMetrics library is used to compute the paper's column-shape and pair-correlation quality metrics.

title: Tabular Data Synthesis with Differential Privacy: A Survey
summary: A survey paper that comprehensively reviews differentially private tabular data synthesis methods, classifying them into statistical and deep-learning approaches across centralized and distributed settings, and comparing them on utility, privacy, and computational cost. It discusses CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and federated variants built on it (Fed-TGAN, DP-CTGAN), and separately notes Patki et al.'s use of Gaussian copulas for relational parent-child synthesis. SDV-family methods (CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and the SDV Gaussian copula relational approach) are discussed and described in prose as prior art, not run experimentally by the authors.
evidence: "Xu et al. [140] proposed a mode-specific normalization based on the Gaussian Mixture Model to capture complex data distributions." and "Patki et al. [106] used Gaussian copulas to capture parent-child relationships."

title: TabularARGN: A Flexible and Efficient Auto-Regressive Framework for Generating High-Fidelity Synthetic Data
summary: This paper from MOSTLY AI introduces TabularARGN, an auto-regressive framework for synthesizing mixed-type, multivariate and sequential tabular data that supports fairness-aware generation, imputation, and flexible conditional sampling on arbitrary column subsets. It is benchmarked against numerous state-of-the-art generators (CTGAN, STaSy, TabSyn, TabMT, ClavaDDPM, RC-TGAN, REaLTabFormer) on both flat and sequential datasets, measuring accuracy, training/generation time, and privacy. SDV's CTGAN and its relational SDV/PARSynthesizer are run as baseline generators, and SDMetrics is used to compute the paper's fidelity metrics (marginal, bivariate, and coherence accuracy).

title: TabularBench: Benchmarking Adversarial Robustness for Tabular Deep Learning in Real-world Use-cases
summary: This preprint introduces TabularBench, the first large-scale benchmark for adversarial robustness of tabular deep-learning classifiers, spanning five real-world scenarios in finance, healthcare, and security with over 200 pre-trained models and 7 robustification mechanisms. The authors augment their real datasets with synthetic tabular data generated by several deep generative models to test robustness with and without data augmentation. CTGAN and TVAE are run as two of several synthetic-data generators (alongside TableGAN, WGAN, GOGGLE, and CutMix) used to produce the augmentation data feeding the adversarial training and evaluation pipeline.

summary: This paper proposes TabularQGAN, a quantum generative adversarial network with flexible data encoding and a novel quantum circuit ansatz for synthesizing heterogeneous tabular data. It is tested on the MIMIC-III healthcare and Adult Census datasets and benchmarked against classical generators (CTGAN, CopulaGAN, VAE-GMM, and an LLM-based approach), evaluated using SDMetrics' overall similarity score and downstream predictive performance. title: Targeted synthetic data generation for tabular data via hardness characterization
summary: This paper proposes a targeted data-augmentation pipeline for tabular binary classification that first identifies 'hard' training points using KNN data Shapley values, then trains a synthetic data generator only on those hardest points, showing improved out-of-sample performance over non-targeted augmentation on simulated, American Express credit, and UCI datasets. The generators used throughout the experiments are CTGAN and TVAE, implemented via a heavily customized, forked version of the sdv and ctgan Python packages with custom early stopping. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE synthesizers, run through a modified fork of the sdv/ctgan libraries, form the empirical backbone of the entire targeted-augmentation study.

summary: This preprint develops a taxonomy of synthetic data use in advanced analytics, categorizing generation approaches (domain knowledge, statistical distribution, deep learning) and identifying typical application scenarios such as sample generation, sample size augmentation, and anonymization, based on a systematic literature review. It aims to assess current adoption and highlight missed research opportunities rather than proposing or running any new synthesizer. The SDV paper is cited only as one of three supporting references for the claim that synthetic data can generate samples, augment data, or anonymize data.

title: DP-TBART: A Transformer-based Autoregressive Model for Differentially Private Tabular Data Generation
summary: This paper introduces DP-TBART, a transformer-based autoregressive model that generates differentially private synthetic tabular data, aiming to close the performance gap between deep-learning and marginal-based DP synthesis methods across ten datasets. The authors compare DP-TBART against marginal-based state-of-the-art (AIM) and several deep-learning baselines including DP-CTGAN, DP-MERF, DP-HFlow, and DP-NTK. title: TraceCodec: A Compiler-Backed Neural Codec for Stateful Multi-Flow Network Traffic Traces

title: TrialSynth: Generation of Synthetic Sequential Clinical Trial Data
summary: TrialSynth is a Variational Autoencoder combined with Hawkes Processes designed to generate synthetic time-sequential clinical trial event data, addressing the challenge of small patient populations where prior static-context synthesizers fall short. The authors benchmark it against seven models including an LSTM VAE, TabDDPM, HALO, and SDV's PARSynthesizer and CTGAN on real-world oncology trial datasets, measuring fidelity, utility, and privacy leakage. SDV's PARSynthesizer (a conditional probabilistic auto-regressive model) and CTGAN are both run as baseline synthesizers, among several others, that TrialSynth is shown to outperform.
affiliations: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; Carle Illinois College of Medicine
evidence: "PARSynthesizer from SDV [33, 48] since it is the most relevant model for synthesizing sequential event data, based on a conditional probabilistic auto-regressive (CPAR) model" -- run as a baseline alongside CTGAN in the comparative results tables (AUCROC, DCR, dataset-inference attack).

title: Trustable and Automated Machine Learning Running with Blockchain and Its Applications
summary: This preprint proposes a blockchain-based framework for trustable and automated machine learning, addressing data immutability and automation via server-layer, streaming-layer, and smart-contract implementations. It also introduces a new synthetic data generation method to enrich training data, demonstrated on fraud detection in financial data. The original SDV paper is cited only in the reference list as prior work on synthetic data generation, with no evidence it was run.
evidence: Reference [26]: 'N. Patki, R. Wedge, K. Veeramachaneni, "The synthetic data vault", Data Science and Advanced Analytics (DSAA) 2016.' No SDV-family term appears outside the reference list.

title: Trustworthy synthetic data for campaign decision support: strategy simulation fidelity and the PolicySynth framework
summary: This paper proposes strategy simulation fidelity (SSF), a decision-alignment metric for evaluating synthetic-data layers in marketing decision support systems, and PolicySynth, a generator conditioned on a production churn scorer to preserve decision-relevant structure. On telecommunications and banking corpora it benchmarks PolicySynth against several tabular generators, reporting mean SSF, seed-to-seed stability, membership-inference risk, and novel-record rate as a joint deployment gate. CTGAN and TVAE are run throughout as comparison baselines, with CTGAN's much wider seed-to-seed variance (SD 0.115 vs PolicySynth's 0.012) forming the paper's central stability argument.
evidence: "PolicySynth attains a mean SSF of 0.923... with seed-to-seed variance roughly ten times tighter than CTGAN on telecommunications and 2.5 times on banking"; Table 1 reports CTGAN and TVAE alongside PolicySynth, TabDDPM, REaLTabFormer and a bootstrap control across all decision-alignment, stability and privacy metrics.
needs: No explicit statement that the sdv-dev/ctgan package (vs. an independent implementation) was used to run CTGAN/TVAE; assumed api-like baseline use given no reimplementation details are given.

title: TSGM: A Flexible Framework for Generative Modeling of Synthetic Time Series
summary: This paper introduces TSGM, an open-source, extensible Python framework for generating and evaluating synthetic time series data, supporting generative, probabilistic, and simulator-based methods along with multi-angle quality evaluation (similarity, downstream effectiveness, privacy, fairness, etc.). In its related-work comparison, the authors describe DeepEcho, part of the SDV ecosystem, as implementing basic GAN and probabilistic autoregressive models for time series, and place it in a feature-comparison table against TSGM and other frameworks. DeepEcho's PAR-style sequential model is discussed and compared on capability grounds but is not run as part of TSGM's own experiments.
affiliations: Aalto University; The University of Manchester
evidence: "Patki et al. [51] introduced an open-source ecosystem for synthetic data generation in different domains; it implements basic GAN and probabilistic autoregressive models for time series in their framework DeepEcho [71]." DeepEcho is also listed with feature checkmarks in a framework-comparison table (Table 1).

title: Turning the Tables: Biased, Imbalanced, Dynamic Tabular Datasets for ML Evaluation
summary: This paper introduces the Bank Account Fraud (BAF) suite, the first publicly available, privacy-preserving, large-scale suite of realistic tabular datasets derived from an anonymized real-world bank account opening fraud detection dataset, designed to stress-test both performance and fairness of ML methods under temporal shift, class imbalance, and controlled biases. The suite's six dataset variants were produced by training 70 CTGAN models via random hyperparameter search on privacy-perturbed applicant data, with omitted hyperparameters left at CTGAN's implementation defaults. CTGAN is run as the core generative engine that produces the entire synthetic dataset suite underlying the paper's contribution.
evidence: "Default values were used for omitted hyperparameters available in CTGAN's [38] implementation" and "we trained 70 CTGAN models" to generate the BAF dataset suite.

title: Undermining Image and Text Classification Algorithms Using Adversarial Attacks
summary: This preprint proposes adversarial attack strategies against machine learning classifiers, combining GANs and SMOTE to generate data that fools text classification models trained on financial fraud data, and applying FGSM perturbations guided by GradCAM to attack a CNN-based face recognition system. The text-classifier attack pipeline uses CTGAN, run with its default hyperparameters (epochs, batch size, generator/discriminator dimensions, noise embedding dimension), to generate additional adversarial data points from cases the classifiers had misclassified. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, is one of the two generative techniques (alongside SMOTE) that directly produce the adversarial data underlying the text-classification attack results.
affiliations: Farragut High School; Oak Ridge National Laboratory
evidence: "We utilize CTGAN with several default parameters, namely epochs, batch size, generator/discriminator dimensions, and noise embedding dimensions" -- with a full hyperparameter table given, confirming the sdv-dev CTGAN package was run to generate adversarial data for the text-classifier attack.

title: Understanding Latent Flow Models for Tabular Data Synthesis: Targets, Paths, and Sampling
summary: This paper presents an empirical study of latent-space flow-matching models for synthetic tabular data, comparing velocity, score, noise, and posterior-matching learning targets under different probability paths and sampling schemes across seven datasets, and distilling practical configuration guidance balancing utility, disclosure risk, and compute budget. It benchmarks its latent flow variants against several standard tabular generators, including CTGAN and TVAE (run via the synthcity implementation), and against TabDDPM and TabSyn. The SDV library is run directly to compute the shape and trend fidelity metrics used throughout the evaluation, while the CTGAN model itself is cited as one of several baseline generative models compared.
evidence: "We used SDV [19] library for shape and trend, and Synthcity [20] for α-precision, β-recall, and Wasserstein distance." CTGAN and TVAE are separately run as baseline generators via the synthcity implementation.
venue: European Conference on Machine Learning and Principles and Practice of Knowledge Discovery in Databases (ECML-PKDD) 2026, Applied Data Science Track
needs: CTGAN/TVAE baselines are explicitly run through the synthcity implementation rather than the sdv-dev package, so the CTGAN integration mechanism for that part is closer to 'inherited' than 'api_user'; only the SDV library's use for shape/trend metrics is unambiguous api_user.

title: A Unified Framework for Quantifying Privacy Risk in Synthetic Data
summary: This paper introduces Anonymeter, an open-source statistical framework that quantifies singling-out, linkability, and inference privacy risks in synthetic tabular data, aligning the evaluation with GDPR's three anonymization criteria. The authors validate the framework through attack-based experiments on synthetic datasets with deliberately inserted leakages and on data generated with and without differential privacy, comparing against prior privacy-evaluation frameworks. CTGAN, run via the original sdv-dev/SDV implementation, is the primary generator used to produce the synthetic datasets (Adults, Texas, US Census) that the entire empirical evaluation of privacy risk is built on, alongside a DP variant (DPCTGAN).
evidence: "We rely on the original implementation of the algorithm" with footnote to https://github.com/sdv-dev/SDV, and 'we use the default hyperparameters as specified in the documentation' citing sdv.dev/SDV/user_guides/single_table/ctgan.html.

title: A Unified Framework for Tabular Generative Modeling: Loss Functions, Benchmarks, and Improved Multi-objective Bayesian Optimization Approaches
summary: This preprint proposes a unified framework for tabular deep generative modeling that adds a correlation- and distribution-aware regularization loss to existing generators, introduces a multi-objective Bayesian optimization strategy (IORBO) for hyperparameter search, and provides a benchmarking protocol across twenty datasets and ten baseline models. The framework is validated by modifying and retraining several generators, including CTGAN, TVAE, and CopulaGAN, with the new loss terms, alongside CTAB-GAN, DP-CGANS, and TabDDPM. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE architectures are directly extended with the authors' custom correlation/distribution loss and evaluated with and without conditional sampling, while CopulaGAN (Gaussian Copula + CTGAN) is run as one of the evaluated generators, making these SDV-family models a load-bearing part of the empirical programme.
evidence: "We extended the TVAE model (Xu et al., 2019) (a VAE designed for tabular data) with the proposed loss function"; CTGAN, CopulaGAN, TVAE all trained with the custom correlation/distribution loss and with conditioning disabled to test the conditional element's impact.
needs: Unclear whether the authors ran the actual sdv-dev/ctgan packages with modified loss hooks or fully reimplemented CTGAN/TVAE/CopulaGAN from scratch in PyTorch; hyperparameter names (embedding_dim, generator_dim, discriminator_dim, etc.) match the sdv-dev CTGAN constructor, suggesting library-based extension rather than pure reimplementation.

title: Unmasking Algorithmic Bias in Predictive Policing: A GAN-Based Simulation Framework with Multi-City Temporal Analysis
summary: This paper presents a reproducible GAN-based simulation framework coupling a spatial GAN with a Noisy-OR patrol-detection model to quantify how racial bias propagates through predictive policing pipelines, using multi-year Baltimore and Chicago crime data alongside Census demographics. Beyond the core bias-audit simulation, the authors evaluate an algorithmic mitigation strategy in which a Conditional Tabular GAN rebalances training data by racial group, finding it shifts but does not eliminate detection disparities. CTGAN, explicitly run via the sdv library (version 1.9.0), is used to generate race-balanced synthetic incident records for this debiasing experiment.
evidence: "GAN training uses PyTorch 2.1; CTGAN uses the sdv library 1.9.0." ... "We replace 30% of the real training incidents with CTGAN-generated incidents drawn in equal proportion..."

title: Towards Useful and Private Synthetic Omics: Community Benchmarking of Generative Models for Transcriptomics Data
summary: A community benchmarking study from the CAMDA 2025 Health Privacy Challenge that systematically evaluates 11 generative methods for synthesizing bulk RNA-seq data across two cancer cohorts, measuring distributional fidelity, downstream utility, biological plausibility, and membership-inference privacy risk. CTGAN, along with a differentially private DP-CTGAN variant, is one of the generative methods benchmarked and is reported to suffer substantial loss of downstream predictive signal and near random-guessing membership inference risk. SDV's CTGAN model is run as one of several evaluation subjects rather than as the paper's own proposed generator.
evidence: "CTGAN variants, together with DP-CVAE, NMF variants, display the lowest relative scores across most metrics... CTGAN and DP-CTGAN, which generally exhibit near random-guessing level membership inference risk."
needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev/CTGAN package or reimplemented with a DP wrapper, so integration marked unclear.

title: On the Usefulness of Synthetic Tabular Data Generation
summary: This workshop paper benchmarks the practical usefulness of synthetic tabular data across four use cases -- data sharing, data augmentation, class balancing, and data summarization -- comparing several deep generative models (CTGAN, TVAE, normalizing flows, and a pretrained LLM-based generator) and concluding there is insufficient evidence that synthetic tabular data reliably improves ML training. Conditional variants of CTGAN and TVAE (from Xu et al., 2019) are trained and evaluated as two of the core generative models across all experiments, though hyperparameter naming in the reported tables suggests a third-party reimplementation rather than the sdv-dev package itself.
evidence: "We include the following state-of-the-art tabular data generation methods... Conditional Tabular GANs (CTGANs) (Xu et al., 2019)... Tabular Variational AutoEncoders (TVAEs) (Xu et al., 2019)." Both are trained as 'Conditional CTGAN' and 'Conditional TVAE' across all four benchmarking use cases.
venue: Data-centric Machine Learning Research (DMLR) Workshop at the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning
needs: Hyperparameter naming in the appendix tables (e.g., discriminator_opt_betas, encoder_max_clusters, clipping_value) resembles a third-party library such as synthcity rather than sdv-dev's ctgan package naming (embedding_dim, generator_dim, etc.), so it is unclear whether SDV's own CTGAN/TVAE code ran or a reimplementation was used.

title: Utility Assessment of Synthetic Data Generation Methods
summary: This paper empirically investigates how different synthetic data generation methods and synthesis parameters affect data utility, comparing a priori metrics against a posteriori analysis accuracy across census-type (Adult, Polish) and other (Avila) datasets, using primarily decision-tree and Synthpop-based synthesizers. In its related-work discussion it describes a prior study that compared four data synthesizers including Data-Synthesizer, Synthpop variants, and the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV), finding Synthpop Non-parametric performed best overall. SDV is only cited as one synthesizer used in a related paper's comparison, not run in this work's own experiments.
evidence: "...used them to compare the utility of four data synthesizers (i.e Data-Synthesizer (DS), Synthetic Data Vault (SDV), Synthpop Parametric, Synthpop Non-parametric)."
needs: SDV is mentioned only as part of describing another paper's (Snoke et al. or similar) comparative study; the current authors do not appear to run SDV themselves.

title: On the Utility Recovery Incapability of Neural Net-based Differential Private Tabular Training Data Synthesizer under Privacy Deregulation
summary: This paper audits the privacy-utility tradeoff of differentially private tabular data synthesizers, showing that DP-CTGAN and PATE-CTGAN fail to recover utility as privacy budgets are relaxed, while the Bayesian-network-based PrivBayes/DataSynthesizer does recover. The experiments run DP-CTGAN and PATE-CTGAN via the SmartNoise library across multiple UCI/Kaggle datasets and classifiers. CTGAN's original paper (Xu et al.) is cited only in a related-work list as the base architecture underlying DP-CTGAN and PATE-CTGAN, with no SDV-package code run.
evidence: "Methods of neural network-based tabular data synthesizer (without differential privacy) include CGAN for tabular data [24], DePart[25], Table-GAN [26], TGAN[27] and CTAB-GAN[28]." DP-CTGAN and PATE-CTGAN, the models actually run, are implemented via the SmartNoise library, not the SDV package.

title: C$^2$VAE: Gaussian Copula-based VAE Differing Disentangled from Coupled Representations with Contrastive Posterior
summary: This paper proposes C2VAE, a self-supervised variational autoencoder that jointly learns disentangled representations via total-correlation-driven factorization and coupled representations via a neural Gaussian copula, using a contrastive classifier to separate the two. It targets improved disentangled representation learning across image and other datasets, addressing instability in TC-based VAE training. CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019) is cited only once in passing, in an undifferentiated list of prior VAE works applied to tabular data.
evidence: "Various VAEs have been proposed in recent years to robustly fit the likelihoods of diverse data, such as tabular data [14, 48, 31, 3, 2], images ... and sequences" — CTGAN appears only as one numbered citation in this list, with no further engagement.

title: Validated Synthetic Patient Generation for Small Longitudinal Cohorts: Coagulation Dynamics Across Pregnancy
summary: This preprint introduces multiplicity-weighted Stochastic Attention (SA), a generative framework based on modern Hopfield networks for synthesizing small longitudinal patient cohorts, applied to 23 patients' coagulation profiles across pregnancy including PCOS and preeclampsia cases. The authors validate SA against statistical, structural, and mechanistic tests, including a blinded coagulation model calibrated on the synthetic data. As a baseline comparison at this small sample size, CTGAN and TVAE (from Xu et al. 2019) are trained on the same 90 per-visit records and shown to suffer mode collapse and fail to capture cross-visit covariance, contrasting with SA's performance.
evidence: "The CTGAN model produced median MREs of approximately 19% across all tested epoch counts (300–3,000), consistent with mode collapse at this sample size. The TVAE model achieved comparable marginal fidelity at high epoch counts..." (Table S6)

title: A Validation Study for Medical Research Based on Synthetic Hospital Data (Preprint)
summary: This preprint reports a cross-hospital validation study assessing whether statistical results from synthetic electronic medical record data reproduce those obtained from real patient data across five clinical research topics. The authors describe an institutional system that generates fictitious-patient synthetic data to let researchers analyze data before IRB approval, finding good accuracy and stability of estimates when sample sizes are large. The work cites the original Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) paper as the basis for its synthetic data generation approach, without detailing which SDV component or code was actually used.

title: Validation-Stage Combinatorial Fusion Analysis for Imbalanced Credit-Card Fraud Detection
summary: This paper studies Combinatorial Fusion Analysis (CFA), a rank-score model-subset selection framework, as a validation-stage method for improving fraud detection on the IEEE-CIS Kaggle benchmark, showing small but reliable gains over the best single gradient-boosted model. Separately, it runs a CTGAN augmentation experiment, training CTGAN on the training-set fraud samples to generate synthetic minority rows for class-balancing, and finds this augmentation degrades both individual classifiers and CFA performance. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, is run directly as a data-augmentation generator and rejected as unhelpful in this setting.

title: VarPPUD: Variant post prioritization developed for undiagnosed genetic disorders
summary: This preprint introduces VarPPUD, a machine-learning tool trained on gene-, amino acid-, and nucleotide-level features to distinguish disease-causing variants from other deleterious candidates prioritized in Undiagnosed Diseases Network (UDN) cases, improving on traditional pathogenicity predictors. To further validate the model, the authors used CTGAN to generate additional synthetic variants from unimputed UDN feature vectors, applying constraint design to keep synthesized values within valid ranges and types. CTGAN is run as an auxiliary data-generation step to test VarPPUD's discriminative ability on synthetic, GAN-generated candidate variants.

title: Watermarking Generative Categorical Data
summary: This paper proposes a statistical framework for watermarking generative categorical data, embedding secret signals at the distribution level by splitting and deterministically modifying one component of the data distribution, and verifying watermarks via an insertion inverse algorithm and total variation distance test. It targets synthetic tabular/categorical data generation broadly, motivated by concerns about provenance and copyright in AI-generated data. CTGAN is cited only in passing, in a list of tabular generative models (alongside TabDDPM and TabSyn) that motivate the need for watermarking, without being run or evaluated in the work.

title: Watermarking Generative Tabular Data
summary: This paper proposes a statistical watermarking mechanism for synthetic tabular data, embedding signals via strategic binning of continuous features and detecting them through a hypothesis-testing framework that requires only a continuous underlying density. It demonstrates theoretical guarantees on fidelity and robustness to additive noise attacks, validated empirically on six real-world datasets. TVAE, from the CTGAN paper, is run as one of three tabular data generators (alongside CTABGAN and TabDDPM) whose synthetic outputs are watermarked and evaluated for fidelity and ML utility.

title: Weakly Augmented Variational Autoencoder in Time Series Anomaly Detection
summary: This work proposes a VAE-based framework for time series anomaly detection that combines self-supervised learning with augmented latent representations, introducing a practical implementation called WAVAE that improves robustness to normal data and sensitivity to anomalies. Experiments on five public synthetic and real datasets show improved ROC-AUC and PR-AUC over state-of-the-art baselines. title: "What do you want from theory alone?" Experimenting with Tight Auditing of Differentially Private Synthetic Data Generation
summary: This paper presents a rigorous auditing framework for differentially private synthetic data generation (DP-SDG) algorithms, using membership inference attacks in black-box and white-box threat models to empirically verify theoretical DP guarantees and uncover real implementation bugs across six DP-SDG systems. The authors find both known and new DP violations, including one in a DPWGAN implementation submitted to the NIST DP Synthetic Data Challenge. title: When Tables Leak: Attacking String Memorization in LLM-Based Tabular Data Generation
summary: This paper introduces LevAtt, a no-box membership inference attack that exploits string-level memorization of numeric digits in LLM-based tabular synthetic data generators, showing severe privacy leakage in models like RealTabFormer and GREaT, and proposes a digit-perturbation defense that trades minimal fidelity/utility loss for reduced leakage. As controls representing conventional (non-LLM) tabular generators, the authors include CT-GAN and TVAE, implemented through the Synthcity library rather than the sdv-dev package, and find these baselines show no leakage under LevAtt since they generate full rows rather than token strings. CTGAN and TVAE, the models introduced in the SDV-family CTGAN paper, are run as control baselines against which the LLM-based attack surface is contrasted.

title: Which is the best model for my data?
summary: This paper proposes a meta-learning approach to select the optimal classifier and hyperparameter configuration for a given tabular classification dataset, using 62 meta-features and a multilabel classifier trained on a meta-dataset built from real and synthetic problems. To enlarge training data, the authors use two synthetic-data generation strategies, one of which is Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN), employed to produce extra training instances from real-world classification problems. CTGAN, with its mode-specific normalization and conditional generator, is run as one of the two data-generation approaches underpinning the empirical meta-dataset.
evidence: "To generate synthetic classification problems from a collection of real-world datasets, we will resort to a generative model, Conditional Tabular GAN (CTGAN), which is introduced and is shown to outperform GAN-based or Bayesian network-based data generation models in [34]."

title: Why LLMs Are Bad at Synthetic Table Generation (and what to do about it)
summary: This paper diagnoses a structural weakness in LLM-based synthetic tabular data generation, showing that autoregressive token generation with random feature-order fine-tuning fails to capture functional dependencies and conditional class-mixtures, and proposes Permutation-aided Fine-tuning (PAFT) to fix this. The authors benchmark PAFT against CTGAN, CopulaGAN, TabSyn, and GReaT on six real and four simulated datasets, evaluating violation rates, ML efficacy, and distributional similarity. CTGAN and CopulaGAN are run as baseline generators via the officially released SDV library API, and SDMetrics' quality-report scores (single-column shape, pairwise trends) are used as core evaluation metrics throughout the empirical comparison.
